blocks.raw: <Tip>The defining distinction: Pre-tensioning = tendons tensioned BEFORE concrete placed. Post-tensioning = tendons tensioned AFTER concrete hardened. This timing difference determines the structural system, production method, and field application. Memorize this clearly to avoid the common reversal error (ERR-STRC-016).</Tip>

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={[ "Reversing pre-tensioning and post-tensioning definitions. Pre = tendons tensioned BEFORE concrete placed. Post = tendons tensioned AFTER concrete hardened. This is the opposite of the common error; verify by physical logic: 'pre' comes before, 'post' comes after.", "Assuming pre-tensioning and post-tensioning have identical structural behavior. Pre-tensioning provides immediate compression (from release onward); post-tensioning requires the concrete to develop strength before compression is applied. The timing affects serviceability, deflection, and crack control.", "Forgetting that post-tensioned ducts must be grouted after tensioning. Ungrouted tendons do not provide full composite action and allow corrosion risk. Grouting bonds the tendon to concrete and protects against corrosion—non-negotiable for permanent service.", "Using ordinary reinforcing bar yield strength (414 MPa) instead of prestressing tendon strength (1,770–1,960 MPa) in calculations. Prestressing relies on the much higher strength of special steel; using lower strength numbers makes the system uneconomical and underperforming." ]} />
